_note: The balance surface of the `consumable` content class (item module 18, spec-consumables.md / ssot-consumables.md G2). Every number a balance pass would touch lives here; nothing structural does. The STRUCTURAL facts stay in code with their AGENTS.md exemption comments and are deliberately absent from this file: grade 1..5 (it is the atom layer's five tiers, not a dial), `manifest_cost >= 1` (a consumable occupying zero manifest places makes the belt limit stop being a limit), and `UnbeltedSlots = 0` (D37 -- an unequipped slot grants nothing, exactly as every other role behaves; a default here would be a carry limit no item earned). See ConsumableLimits.
_carryLimitNote: ⛔ THERE IS NO CARRY LIMIT IN THIS FILE, DELIBERATELY. ssot-consumables.md §10.1 proposed `N = 2` and called it 'the single most consequential number here'. D37 (owner, 2026-09-04: 'add bag feature like diablo belt') withdrew it: the limit is the equipped `girdle`'s own `consumableSlots`, which is CONTENT on a base type (module 6) -- a drop worth finding, not a config row. Putting an N back here would re-impose the global ceiling D37 removed, and it would be a hard progression ceiling of exactly the kind AGENTS.md forbids.
_classesAuthoredNote: ssot-consumables.md §3.1's v1 column. The other three (`board`, `revive`, `utility`) are DECLARED in the closed enum and ungenerated -- the same disposition D14 gave `standard`. A row naming one is refused by name (`consumable.class-unavailable`) rather than silently loaded, because each class names an EXECUTOR and the three unauthored ones have none: `board` waits on an overlay use affordance plus `capPerMatch` (G4), `revive` on the battle-mode use moment (the action layer), `utility` on a menu executor. Widening this list is how a class ships once its executor does -- a one-line edit here, no code change.
_contextsAuthoredNote: ssot-consumables.md §5.2. `battle` was ADDED 2026-09-05 once its host became real: §6.2 code 4's reason for refusing it was 'battle before the action layer' -- `LeafId.HoldsStock` reads the precondition (action-todo.md T10, 2026-08-28) and `ActionCompiler` lifts the demand out of the condition tree, both real. **Correction, 2026-09-07 (base-defense session 5): the commit-time spend this note originally claimed as done ('IStockLedger/RpgStore.TrySpendStock take the stack at commit... the action layer now serves it end to end') was NOT actually wired** -- a precise class-name grep (`grep -rln "ActionStockCommit" src/`) finds exactly one file, its own declaration; `new ActionStockCommit(` is constructed ONLY in test files anywhere in the repo. `RpgStoreStockLedger` (the real `IStockLedger` impl) exists and is unit-tested, but nothing in the live action-commit path (`ActionRunner`/`Bag.OnEvent`) ever constructs an `ActionStockCommit` or calls it -- so a `battle`-context consumable with a real `holdsStock` demand fires for free today, exactly the `NoStockLedger` doc comment's own named risk ('would hand out unlimited free consumables'). This is a genuine, live gap in the `action` program's own scope (see [[action-program]] memory), not base-defense's to fix -- flagged here because this file's own note is what claimed it closed. `lawn` STAYS refused, and for its own reason rather than by association -- spec-usability-conditions.md §3a's mode matrix makes it not bindable at all (the overlay is a stateless observer and never reads current inventory; `ActionCompiler` refuses it by name with `ConsumableUnsupportedInMode`), and `capPerMatch` (G4, §9 item 12a) still has no implementation. Widening is ADDITIVE and never invalidates an authored row, which is the whole no-migration proof (§4.1).
_gradeTierMapNote: MIRRORED, value for value, from data/seed/items/_registry/bands.v1.json's frozen `powerBand.tierMap`. Core never reads a file (tunables-ssot.md §7.2), so the host injects it here -- the same device module 14 used for the cost-band multipliers. `ConsumableCorpusTests.The_grade_tier_map_mirrors_the_frozen_registry_value_for_value` reads the REAL registry, asserts it is still frozen, and compares every pair, so a drift is a red test rather than a silently re-graded corpus. This is what makes ssot-consumables.md §5.2's 'grade MUST equal the tier of every core atom' checkable against a seed that authors a band and never a tier.
_authoringCeilingNote: ssot-consumables.md §4.4's 'authoring budget of <= 10% of a fully-geared actor's contribution (illustrative, unverified)'. BOUNDED RATIO in per-mille (0..1000), and it bounds a REPORT, never an import refusal -- the same disposition module 17 gave its parity band on the day it first became measurable. Refusing 60 authored rows against a ceiling no author was given a way to see would be a validator invented after the fact. It is here so the number a balance pass moves is one file save, and so the report's threshold is not a literal in a metric.
_draughtBindingPriorityNote: ssot-consumables.md §4.3 / §9 item 10: the run-start snapshot binds at `player:{id}` with `slot = NULL` and this priority, MIRRORING charms exactly (ssot-charms.md:319-328) -- 'one snapshot mechanism, two sources; whoever builds it first owns it and the other adopts it'. This module builds it first (module 22 `charm-carry` is unbuilt), so `source` is the only difference between the two. A balance pass that reorders the run-start layer relative to equipment moves this number; it must move the charm side with it, which is why the note says so here rather than in a comment nobody reads.
